reassignInfo.label: Reassign absent member
reassignInfo.title: What is it and what happens when you request a reassignment?
points: It replaces a teammate who won't take part (didn't show up or has gone silent).
It takes TWO team members: the request isn't executed until a second teammate confirms the same reassignment.
Once that agreement is reached, that person is marked absent and removed from your team and from the hackathon. The action is immediate and irreversible.
The system automatically picks the first candidate from the reserve pool (by registration order) and adds them to your team in their place.
If the pool is empty, your team continues with 3 members (the allowed minimum) and the organizers are notified.
It's only available during the building phase.

why.label: what is nan
why.lead: Builders sharing dedicated GPUs to run open models and burn tokens without limits.
p: Closed-model APIs are convenient but expensive and limited. Open models are free but running them seriously requires hardware almost no one has at home.
NaN solves this by sharing powerful GPUs among builders who actually use them, splitting the real cost of infrastructure.
A closed community by design, limited to the real capacity of shared GPUs. When it fills up, we open a waitlist.
The community lives on Discord. The website only manages access. Every member pays to be here. Only those who truly want to build make it in.

who.label: who's behind
who.title: The NaN community is led by Cristian Córdova and Borja Perez.
who.quote: I started NaN because I wanted to run serious open models without usage limits, and share and learn with people in the same boat: builders who actually burn tokens.
cristianBio: Founder of Helmcode, working with startups on cloud infrastructure, AI tooling and open source.
Thanks to Helmcode we offer open model inference with unlimited token plans for enterprises. I share my experiments on social media and AI research.
borjaBio: Builder with marketing skills. Helping Cristian with comms and community.
Our goal is to create the best open-models community in the world, helping people create and ship products with open AI.

items.a: A closed community of builders sharing dedicated GPUs to run open models. Every member pays to be here, and there's only room for people who actually build.
The models run 24/7 on a shared inference cluster. Each member gets a personal API key compatible with OpenAI: change the base_url and you're in.

On the cluster models, no counter. The frontier ones come with a token allowance per member so the plan holds up: 2B tokens per month on DeepSeek V4-Flash, 1.0B per month on MiMo v2.5, 1B per month on Qwen 3.8 Flash, 500M per month on GLM 5.3 Flash, and 3,000M per billing period on GLM 5.2 for members on the premium tier. Those limits are published here, not in fine print. The bill is the fixed subscription price and it doesn’t move.

Every quarter members vote on Discord which new models join the cluster. Candidates are pre-selected technically: they have to fit the real capacity. The open ecosystem moves fast, and so does the cluster.
Processed in the European Union, with no logging of prompts or responses. Your API key is personal and non-transferable. Your code trains no model and your data never leaves your session.

Builders who want to run open models seriously without building the infrastructure: indie hackers, makers, people with agents and side projects in production. It's not for someone who just wants to try a couple of prompts.
Because they can be audited, modified and used without asking permission. Closed ones are convenient but create dependency. With open models, the stack is yours.
No. NaN is inference, not training. The GPUs are optimized to run existing models at high speed, not for fine-tuning.

items.q: What payment methods do you accept?
items.a: Credit or debit card. New memberships are billed in euros from any region, taxes included; subscriptions opened earlier in US dollars keep their original price. No commitment: cancel anytime.
Leave your email on the waitlist and we'll write when a spot opens. There's a waitlist because there are no more GPUs: when compute comes in, people come in.

context.title: Someone asked an agent for a Call of Duty.
context.lead: Not once. They built a loop: sub-agents each owning one piece, and a critic comparing the result against the real game that refused to sign off until you couldn't tell them apart. That is a Gauntlet Loop, and it's what the workshop opening August takes apart. The challenge is that everyone builds their own.

survey.metaTitle: The answers from the NaN builders
survey.metaDesc: We asked what you need in NaN. And this is what you answered. In the tab above you will find part of the roadmap we are going to work on over the coming months.
survey.lead: We asked what you need in NaN. And this is what you answered. In the tab above you will find part of the roadmap we are going to work on over the coming months.
survey.dataLead: Multi-select questions allowed several answers, so the percentages add up to more than 100. In the open questions, free text has been grouped into themes and one answer can count in several. The base is stated on every chart.
survey.roadmapHead: What we are going to do
survey.roadmapLead: Part of the roadmap for the coming months, taken from what you answered. At the end you will find the options we are still weighing up: those are not a commitment, they are the ones we want to talk through with you.
method: Method. 78 answers collected between 13 and 20 August 2026 in the form “We are planning the future of NaN”. The charts show percentages only, over the base stated in each header. Multi-select questions were tabulated against the form's option list, separating the free text that gets mixed into the same cell; that is why “others” is commented separately instead of counted as an option. Open questions were grouped into themes by hand and one answer can fall into several, so those percentages do not add up to 100.

Privacy. Quotes carry no name and no response number, and any quote that would make someone recognisable has been left out. No projects, addresses, emails or contact details are published here: the permission given was for Built with NaN, not for this report.

Biases to keep in mind. The sample is self selected, so the people who answer are the most involved and quiet discontent is under represented. The cancellation reason was single choice, which forces one pick when almost a quarter needed to write their own. And the cross tabs by time zone or by product in production rest on small groups: the direction is clear, the magnitude is not precise.
survey.closing: This is not a closed list. If something you care about is missing, say so: the survey was the starting point, not the end. We will announce things as they land, through the usual channels.
